rule.description: The cohesive per-page column statistics record (maximum value, minimum value, null count) is dispersed: its members travel through the parquet write pipeline as individually threaded carriers instead of inside one grouping. A production symbol in the page/chunk layout packages or the writer packages matches when its signature (parameters plus results, receiver excluded) holds at least two statistics value carriers (interface{}, []interface{}, map[K][]interface{}) together with at least one null-count carrier (*int64, []*int64, map[K][]*int64), or when its owning record type holds two or more statistics value collections together with at least one null-count collection. Detection reads type shapes only; renames of members never remove a match, and grouping the three members into one abstraction at every collated site removes all matches.

checks.description: Detect write-path functions and methods whose parameters or results carry the page-statistics record as individually threaded members: at least two statistics value carriers together with at least one null-count carrier in one signature.
checks.detected_relation: write-path function or method signature -> separately threaded statistics value carriers plus null-count carrier
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The maximum, minimum, and null count of one page are one record, yet each of these signatures makes its members cross the interface as independent values, so every call site repeats the grouping by hand and every new statistic widens the whole chain.

matches.evidence: Slicing a plain column table returns pages plus three parallel per-page aggregates ([]interface{} maxima, []interface{} minima, []*int64 null counts, nil entries under omitstats) alongside the total size.
v1 data-page serialization takes the page maximum, minimum, and null count as three separate scalar inputs (interface{}, interface{}, *int64) instead of reading a grouped record.
The v2-header compatibility form takes the same three members as separate scalar inputs, so both header forms thread the record ungrouped.
The dictionary-encoded slicer returns pages plus the same three parallel per-page aggregates, so the sibling production paths both emit the record ungrouped.
Dictionary-encoded data-page serialization takes the three members as separate scalar inputs; the dictionary page itself stays out of the statistics flow.
Plain chunk aggregation receives per-page maxima, minima, and null counts as three separate index-aligned slices and folds them into chunk metadata.
Dictionary chunk aggregation receives the same three separate index-aligned slices and must skip the caller-supplied null member at the dictionary-page position by convention.

checks.description: Detect record types in the writer that hold the buffered per-column statistics as parallel collections: two or more statistics value collections plus at least one null-count collection on one owner.
checks.detected_relation: pipeline owner record -> per-column statistics value collections plus per-column null-count collection
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The writer buffers each column's page statistics next to its page buffer, split across parallel per-column collections whose lengths and order must be kept equal to the page buffer by convention at every append, merge, and reset, instead of buffering the record with its pages.

matches.evidence: ParquetWriter keeps MaxValsBuf, MinValsBuf (map[string][]interface{}) and NullCntsBuf (map[string][]*int64) beside PagesMapBuf; the value-carrier count is 3 because the pre-existing Objs buffer field also has the []interface{} carrier shape and is counted by the type-shape rule without regard to names. flushObjs threads per-worker maps of the three collections through the parallel-flush merge, appends them name-by-name into the per-column buffers, and Flush consumes them at row-group assembly (prepending a fabricated nil member for a dictionary-page position) before resetting all four maps; both NewParquetWriter and the arrow adapter's NewArrowWriter must allocate the new collections separately.

excluded.reason: Page decoding and column buffers never materialize per-page statistics; the record exists only on the write path, so the rule is scoped there.

The thrift structs (Statistics, ColumnMetaData, ColumnIndex) are the serialized file-format boundary the record's members must fill; they are not in-flight carriers and regrouping generated serialization types is not a valid repair surface.
Dictionary pages carry no statistics on this write path; threading the record there would fabricate dead carriers.
Serializes the dictionary page header, which has no statistics in either state.
Row-group column-index construction consumes the already-serialized page-header Statistics, not the in-flight record, so grouping there is moot.

The per-type accumulation helpers take and return bare interface{} min/max values but carry no null-count member, so their shape does not satisfy the rule and they are value-only helpers of the record's members.
Adapters forward records into the base writer without touching the statistics record.
